planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; this lavandin grows much larger than 'Hidcote' English lavender, so give it significantly more room to spread.

directions: Despite sharing part of its name with the compact English lavender 'Hidcote', this lavandin selection is one of the largest and most robust cultivars grown, forming a substantial mound of silvery foliage topped by long, deep violet-blue flower spikes in midsummer. Plant in lean, alkaline, fast-draining soil and resist the urge to crowd it, since it needs real elbow room to develop its characteristic broad habit. Cut spent flower stems back hard after the main bloom to prevent the woody center from splitting open, and avoid winter-wet sites that encourage root and crown rot. Its long stems and heavy flower yield make it a favorite among growers producing dried lavender bundles and craft bouquets.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container-grown plants in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; propagate vegetatively since named English lavender selections do not come true from seed.

directions: This compact English lavender selection forms a neat, rounded mound of narrow gray-green leaves and sends up short, dense spikes of rich violet-blue flowers in early to midsummer. Site it in gritty, lean soil with excellent drainage, since like other English lavenders it declines quickly in heavy clay or over-irrigated beds. Shear lightly right after the first flush of bloom to keep the mound tight and encourage a second, lighter round of flowers later in the season. Its small stature suits border edging, dry rock gardens, and containers where larger lavandin types would be out of scale.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; soft pink flower color holds best with some relief from the most intense afternoon heat.

directions: A dwarf English lavender grown for its soft pale pink flower spikes, an unusual break from the blue and violet tones typical of the species, held above a tight, compact mound of narrow silver-gray leaves. Grow in sharply drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun, since wet feet quickly cause crown rot in all English lavender selections. Trim back lightly after the main bloom flush to keep the plant dense and prevent legginess, and avoid rich fertilizer, which pushes soft growth at the expense of flowering. Its diminutive size makes it well suited to edging, rock gardens, and small containers.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; this lavandin is grown mainly for its unusual pink flower color rather than for oil production.

directions: Unlike most lavandins, which bloom in shades of blue and violet, this selection produces long spikes of soft pink flowers above a broad mound of gray-green foliage, making it a distinctive accent among typical lavender plantings. Give it lean, fast-draining, slightly alkaline soil and full sun, and avoid overhead irrigation that keeps foliage and crowns damp. Cut the plant back by about a third after the main summer flowering flush to maintain a rounded shape and discourage the center from becoming bare and woody. Its larger size compared to English lavenders means it needs more room to spread than compact border selections.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; its dwarf, dense habit makes it well suited to tight edging and low hedges.

directions: One of the more diminutive English lavender selections, this cultivar forms a tight, dense dome of narrow gray foliage topped in summer by short, deep violet-blue flower spikes. Plant in gritty, lean, well-drained soil in full sun, since like all English lavenders it suffers in heavy or consistently moist ground. Shear lightly right after flowering to maintain the compact dome shape and discourage the woody, open-centered look that older lavender plants can develop. Its small, uniform size makes it a strong candidate for low edging or a miniature lavender hedge along a path.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; this old selection is one of the traditional strains grown for essential-oil distillation in France and England.

directions: A long-cultivated English lavender strain valued historically for the quality and sweetness of its essential oil, forming an upright mound of silvery foliage topped with violet-blue flower spikes in midsummer. Grow in lean, alkaline, sharply drained soil in full sun, since this old strain shows the same intolerance of wet feet as modern named cultivars. Harvest flower spikes just as the lowest florets open for the strongest fragrance, whether for oil, sachets, or dried arrangements. Shear the plant back after flowering to keep growth dense and productive for future seasons.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; one of the oldest pink-flowered English lavender selections still in cultivation.

directions: A classic old English lavender selection grown for its soft pink flower spikes, a gentle contrast to the violet-blue tones typical of the species, carried above compact gray-green foliage. Plant in lean, fast-draining, slightly alkaline soil in full sun, and avoid rich or consistently damp beds that encourage floppy growth and root rot. Shear lightly after the main flowering flush to keep the mound tidy and promote a possible light rebloom later in the season. Its soft coloring works well in cottage borders and pastel plantings where the usual lavender-blue would clash.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; distinct from the dwarf white selection 'Nana Alba' in being a full-size white-flowered form.

directions: A traditional white-flowered English lavender that grows to full standard size, unlike the dwarf 'Nana Alba', producing upright gray-green spikes topped with pure white flowers in midsummer. Grow in gritty, lean soil with excellent drainage and full sun exposure, since white-flowered lavender forms show the same susceptibility to winter wet and root rot as their purple-flowered relatives. Shear the plant back after flowering to maintain a dense, rounded habit and prevent the base from becoming woody and sparse. Its clean white spikes make an effective contrast planting alongside blue- and purple-flowered lavender cultivars in a mixed border.
